speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: And if Ms Tin is satisfied with the answer, she could perhaps withdraw the question for tomorrow.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I will leave the second part to Ms Tin.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But I agree to the merger of Question Nos 1 and 2, for them to be taken together.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, I will start off with the question by Ms Tin Pei Ling.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: She asked about the terrorism threat assessment in ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The terrorism threat in Southeast Asia is serious and persistent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition to terrorist groups like Al-Qaeda and its regional affiliates such as the Jemaah Islamiyah, the conflict in Syria and Iraq and the emergence of the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS) have significantly raised the threat level.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ISIS has attracted many foreign fighters to its ranks.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over 70 of them may have died in the fighting, several as suicide bombers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, several self-radicalised Southeast Asians who were unable to travel to Syria or Iraq to fight have heeded the call by ISIS to carry out terrorist attacks in their home countries in pursuit of the ISIS cause to expand its self-proclaimed "caliphate".

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even then, four Indonesian ISIS supporters succeeded in carrying out a terrorist attack in downtown Jakarta on 14 January this year.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Southeast Asian fighters pose a serious security threat when they return with battlefield experience from Syria and Iraq.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A sizeable number of them have formed a dedicated group in Syria called the Katibah Nusantara lid Daulah Islamiyah or Malay Archipelago Unit for ISIS.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can be expected to use the fighting experience that they have acquired to carry out terrorist attacks in this region.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: ISIS declared in November 2014 its intention to set up "wilayat" or provinces in Indonesia and the Philippines.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The establishment of an ISIS "wilayat" in Southeast Asia would further raise the terrorism threat to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Last year, four Singaporeans were detained and a fifth was issued a Restriction Order, on the basis that they intended to fight for ISIS in Syria and Iraq.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One of those detained had planned to carry out terrorist attacks in Singapore on behalf of ISIS if he was unable to travel overseas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are others who have expressed interest to go to Syria to fight and have been investigated or are currently under investigation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Most of them were radicalised by online videos and articles, and through social media postings.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This problem of self-radicalisation continues to be a concern in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The global and regional terrorism situation is worrying.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The recent attacks in Paris and in Jakarta involved multiple gunmen carrying explosives and heavy firearms, targeting soft targets packed with people who have little or no security protection, and with the aim of inflicting maximum casualties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Against this heightened threat environment, the Home Team has adopted a multi-pronged approach, and I would like to highlight three key measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, Singapore is a major transport hub in the region.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: More than half a million people pass through our checkpoints every day.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our Woodlands checkpoint is the busiest land checkpoint in the world.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Attackers can gather and plan just outside Singapore before coming into Singapore to carry out the attack.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This would be similar to the attacks on Paris, where the planning and preparation were probably carried out in Molenbeek where security was less tight.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Border control is therefore our first line of defence to prevent an attack from taking place in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) therefore conducts checks on travellers, vehicles, baggage and cargo at all our air, land and sea checkpoints and puts in place visible deterrent measures to detect and deny attempts to smuggle prohibited items or persons.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Police Coast Guard has also increased its patrols along our coastline and will be developing a more comprehensive set of physical barriers that will complement these coastal patrols.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to assess the threat level and adjust the security measures at our borders accordingly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But as Ms Joan Pereira's question has suggested, it is a constant challenge to manage the balance between maintaining vigilance and security at our checkpoints and facilitating speedy and efficient travel, especially in the current heightened threat environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of the enhanced security measures at the land check points will cause inconvenience to travellers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is especially so during festive seasons and holidays like the upcoming Chinese New Year period, when traveller volume is expected to increase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are making further investments in technology to help us maintain a high level of security at our checkpoints, while facilitating efficient travel.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For instance, ICA will implement the BioScreen initiative across all checkpoints to capture the fingerprints of all arriving persons by June 2016.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These records will allow us to verify the traveller's identity before he is allowed entry to Singapore and will facilitate automated self-clearance during his departure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under the current heightened threat environment, our security agencies will continue to work closely with international and regional security partners through the exchange of intelligence and information to more effectively combat terrorism.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Police have also enhanced security measures and vigilance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Police have also stepped-up patrols in crowded areas and conducted exercises to raise the level of preparedness of its officers in response to a terrorist attack.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Participants were not informed prior to this surprise exercise in order to test their response.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also work with commercial and private establishments to enhance security measures at their premises.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One platform is the Safety and Security Watch Group (SSWG).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Through SSWG, the Police and the business community have forged a close partnership to counter the threat posed by terrorism.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Building managers or owners and security personnel work together with the Police to assess localised threats, share knowledge and pool resources to enhance their security.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Response protocols are drawn up to deal with crisis situations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Tabletop exercises and live exercises are also being carried to test the plans and validate and refine the contingency plans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Police will continue to assess the threat level and step-up patrols when necessary.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Even as we enhance security at our borders and within Singapore, Government efforts alone will not be adequate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Dealing with terrorism is not just about action by security forces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Each and every one of us has an important part to play.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We must be more alert to help prevent a terrorist attack from happening.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Should an attack take place, we must be able to respond in a number of ways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Above all, when a terrorist attack happens, we must stay united and resilient as one people.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This was indeed the tenor of many speeches in the course of the debate on the President's Address these past few days.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will conduct regular and realistic exercises to help various community groups to be better prepared for and to remain resilient in the aftermath of any attack.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Terrorists seek to threaten our security and our way of life.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They seek to instil fear and divide the community.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Should a terrorist attack occur, it is important for all of us to stand united against these threats, with a spirit of resilience and determination that we should not be defeated.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If MHA's view is that the CCTV footage provided significant evidence, how can we deploy such technology and strategy in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, on 25 January, Monday evening, Channel NewsAsia's Saifulbahari Ismail interviewed the Jakarta Police Chief on television, and he mentioned that he would like to see better CCTV and digital coverage of the city that would enable security forces to better deal with the situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: CCTV and video coverage or the leverage of technology as it advances can achieve a couple of things.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second is	 detection, and especially with analytics, you might be able to, through technology, analyse and detect certain patterns of behaviour.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you have a "live" feed as a situation unfolds, security forces will have a better feel on what is happening on the ground.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Lastly, as the Member has alluded to, post-incident management, not only in the cold light of day or aftermath, but in the tension and the ambiguity as to whether the situation has ended or still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are studying the possibility of putting more cameras in public areas – the study is still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have been working and will continue to work with agencies such as the Land Transport Authority (LTA) to leverage on CCTV cameras that are already out there in the public, and leverage on existing cameras that other agencies use for various purposes in order to help us in our counter-terror efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also work with private and commercial premises and businesses – I spoke earlier about the SSWG.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Under this effort, Police will work with them and engage them to install video surveillance systems, to allow access and to expand coverage.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In addition to localised clusters, we also work with specific industry sectors, for example, with the chemical sector, the security sector, the hotel sector and with F&B, amongst others to help them harden what would otherwise be potentially soft targets.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Lastly, members of the public – you and I – can play a role.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If you have not downloaded it, please do.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It allows people to submit videos, photographs, information to the Police.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It allows close to real time analysis of videos.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We also have a scheme known as Vehicles on Watch (VOW) where members of the public keep their vehicle cameras on in the cars.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That helps to just add extra layers of vigilance.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: Can the Senior Member of State brief the House on counter-terrorism measures relating to air and sea and port facilities, like the air marshal programme and the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS)?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There are certain security measures which, for operational reasons, would not be appropriate for me to share in a public forum such as this.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But I have spoken about the importance of border security.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I had spoken earlier about land, sea and air checkpoints.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They have enhanced and perform very thorough checks on all arriving as well as departing travellers, whether it is through our checkpoints on land, both Woodlands and Tuas, through the air, through Changi and Seletar, as well as through sea, through ports.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But beyond checkpoints, we are also concerned about unauthorised entry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, our physical borders, not just our checkpoints, are also places that remain vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Coast Guard and ICA have enhanced patrols and vigilance.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Physical barriers have been and will continue to be erected as an additional barrier to entry.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Air security is something that is not just of concern to us in Singapore, but certainly, the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and many other agencies internationally, as well as other countries, cooperate very closely and we are plugged into those efforts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, he mentioned earlier, of course, the threat of self-radicalised terrorists but he did not elaborate in his answer very much about the Government's strategies to counter that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I wonder if he could share with us what the Government is doing in that area.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For example, is it making a concerted attempt to block, for example, dangerous Internet sites from being accessible from here?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Within the parameters of the caveat that I gave to the earlier Member, let me deal with Ms Sylvia Lim's questions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First is on self-radicalisation and what the Government has been doing and willing to do.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is, in fact, a Parliamentary Question (PQ) tomorrow set down in the Order Paper, and there will be a comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I urge the Member to be patient.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There will be a more thorough exposition of the issue tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Naturally, there will also be selective checks depending on intelligence and other information.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member asked about the capacity to deal with these threats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, the Home Team needs to be on top of it – needs to be prepared, needs to project, and needs to evolve along the way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In fact, the hon Member, Mr de Souza, will ask that question later.
